newsitem.title: USA: Pioneer up, DeKalb down on patent news.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer up, DeKalb down on patent news.

text.p: Shares of Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc rose 7/8 to 69-3/8 after the company said it was being allowed to include broad claims in a U.S. patent application pending on the genetic transformation of corn.
Shares of seed company rival DeKalb Genetics Corp fell 1-1/2 at 45-3/4.
"It (the patent application) makes Pioneer's case stronger and DeKalb's case not so strong -- that's the initial market knee-jerk reaction," Piper Jaffray analyst George Dahlman said.
He cautioned, however, that there are complex patent claims covering genetic transformation of crops such as corn.
Using genetic manipulation, seed companies can produce crops that are resistant to certain herbicides, and enabling them to fight off certain insects.
DeKalb has a patent infringement lawsuit pending against Pioneer and other agricultural companies.
"We still believe that both sides are going to end up negotiating something," Dahlman said, referring to biotechnology held by Pioneer and DeKalb.
